blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: The factor theorem is the special case of the remainder theorem when the remainder is zero. For numbers, 3 is a factor of 12 because \(12 \div 3\) leaves remainder 0. In the same way \(x - a\) is a factor of \(f(x)\) when dividing by it leaves remainder 0, and by the remainder theorem that remainder is \(f(a)\).

The polynomial \(x - a\) is a factor of the polynomial \(f(x)\) iff \(f(a) = 0\). In other words \(x - a\) is a factor of \(f(x)\) if and only if \(x = a\) is the root of the polynomial equation \(f(x) = 0\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
"iff" is short for "if and only if". It means two facts in one sentence:
1. If \(f(a) = 0\), then \(x - a\) is a factor.
2. If \(x - a\) is a factor, then \(f(a) = 0\).
So to test a factor we only evaluate; to find unknowns we set \(f(a) = 0\) for each known factor. A value \(a\) with \(f(a) = 0\) is also called a root (or zero) of \(f\).

Suppose \(q(x)\) is the quotient and \(R\) is the remainder when a polynomial \(f(x)\) is divided by \(x - a\), till no \(x\)-term exists in the remainder, then by remainder theorem
\[f(x) = (x - a)\,q(x) + R\]

Suppose \(f(a) = 0 \Rightarrow R = 0\)
\[f(x) = (x - a)\,q(x)\]
\((x - a)\) is a factor of \(f(x)\).

Conversely, if \((x - a)\) is a factor of \(f(x)\), then \(f(x) = (x - a)q(x)\) for some polynomial \(q(x)\)
\[f(a) = 0\]
which proves the theorem.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: In the first part, \(R = 0\) because the remainder theorem gives \(R = f(a)\) and \(f(a) = 0\). In the converse, put \(x = a\) in \(f(x) = (x - a)q(x)\): \(f(a) = (a - a)q(a) = 0 \cdot q(a) = 0\).

blocks.title: Example 5
blocks.problem: Show that \(x - 2\) is a factor of \(f(x) = x^{3} - 7x + 6\) without factorizing.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = x^{3} - 7x + 6\) and the linear polynomial \(x - 2\).
To prove: \(x - 2\) is a factor of \(f(x)\), without factorizing.
Method: factor theorem. \(x - 2\) is a factor exactly when \(f(2) = 0\).

Step 1: Find \(a\)
\[x - a = x - 2 \Rightarrow a = 2\]
Why: we compare the divisor with \(x - a\).

Step 2: Evaluate \(f(2)\)
\[f(2) = 2^{3} - 7(2) + 6\]
\[= 8 - 14 + 6 = 0\]
Why: by the factor theorem we only need the value of \(f\) at \(a = 2\).

Step 3: Conclusion
Since \(f(2) = 0\), \(x - 2\) is a factor of \(f(x)\).
Why: \(f(a) = 0\) is exactly the condition of the factor theorem.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: To determine if a given linear polynomial \(x - a\) is a factor of \(f(x)\), we need to check whether \(f(a) = 0\).

blocks.title: Example 6
blocks.problem: If \(x + 1\) and \(x - 2\) are factors of \(x^{3} + px^{2} + qx + 2\). Find the values of \(p\) and \(q\).
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = x^{3} + px^{2} + qx + 2\) with factors \(x + 1\) and \(x - 2\).
To find: \(p\) and \(q\).
Method: factor theorem gives \(f(-1) = 0\) and \(f(2) = 0\). These are two equations in the two unknowns \(p\) and \(q\); solve them simultaneously.

Step 2: Use the factor \(x - 2\)
\[f(2) = 0\]
\[8 + 4p + 2q + 2 = 0\]
\[4p + 2q = -10\]
\[2p + q = -5 \quad \text{...(ii)}\]
Why: \(a = 2\); \(2^{3} = 8\), \(p(2)^{2} = 4p\), \(q(2) = 2q\). Dividing by 2 keeps the numbers small.

Step 3: Add (i) and (ii)
\[(p - q) + (2p + q) = -1 + (-5)\]
\[3p = -6\]
\[p = -2\]
Why: \(-q\) and \(+q\) cancel when we add, leaving one unknown.

Step 4: Find \(q\)
Put \(p = -2\) in (i):
\[q = p + 1 = -2 + 1 = -1\]
Why: from (i), \(p - q = -1\) gives \(q = p + 1\).

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
1. Factor theorem: \(x - a\) is a factor of \(f(x)\) if and only if \(f(a) = 0\).
2. "\(x - a\) is a factor", "\(f(a) = 0\)", "\(a\) is a root of \(f(x) = 0\)" and "remainder 0" all say the same thing.
3. To test a factor, evaluate; to find unknown coefficients, write \(f(a) = 0\) for each given factor and solve.
4. Two unknowns need two equations, so two factors are given in Example 6.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.text:
1. Using \(f(1)\) for the factor \(x + 1\); the correct value is \(f(-1)\).
2. Sign slips with \(q(-1) = -q\) and \(p(-1)^{2} = +p\).
3. Stopping at "\(f(a) = 0\)" without writing the conclusion "therefore \(x - a\) is a factor".
